notes:
=== CONCEPT ===
Netcat manual banner grab captures raw service output that Nmap's version detection may normalize or truncate. The raw banner often contains OS distribution, exact software version, and configuration details that parsed Nmap output suppresses.

=== EXAMPLE ===
SMTP banner via nc: '220 inlane ESMTP Postfix (Ubuntu)' — includes OS distribution. Nmap reports only 'Postfix smtpd'. The raw banner exposes more than the parsed result — always manually grab banners on interesting services.

=== CHAINING ===
nmap port scan identifies open service → nc banner grab reveals exact version/OS → CVE lookup → targeted exploitation.

=== TCPDUMP PAIRING ===
Run tcpdump in parallel with nc to observe the TCP exchange at packet level. The PSH-ACK from the server carries the banner — visible in tcpdump output. Reveals protocol-level behavior that tools suppress.
